To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified, cloned, expressed and characterized a novel soluble flavoprotein reductorase from B. megateriurn, which is able to support the activity of two different P450s and, thus, can be used to establish efficient whole-cell P450 biocatalytic systems.

we identified, expressed and purified a novel soluble NAPDH-dependent diflavin flavoprotein reudctase from Bacillus megeterium, which is able to act as a cytochrome P 450 reductase and to support the hydroxylations of testosterone and progrestone with CYP21A 2 and CYP106A 1, respectively.
we have identified, expressed, purified and characterized the novel B. megaterum CPR (BmCpr) which can be used to establish whole cell biotransformation system with CYP106 and CYP21.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of the molecular basis of the interaction between a novel NADPH-dependent reductase from B. megaterum, BmCPR, and two different cytochrome P-450s, the bacterial CYP106A and the eukaryotic CYP21A.
the development of a novel whole-cell biotansformation system based on a novel bacterial cytochrome P 450 (CYP) reductase.
the identification and characterization, as well as the biotechnological utilization of a novel NADPH-dependent cytochrome P-450 reductase from B. megaterum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the B. megateriun NADPH-dependent cytochrome P-450 reductase is a novel soluble flavin reductase with the ability to transfer electrons to both bacterial and microsomal cytochrome P 450 enzymes.
BmCPR can be used as a novel and promising electron transfer protein for CYP106A- and CYP2A1-based whole cell biotransformation system.

this novel NADPH-dependent BmCPR from B. megaterum represents a novel, soluble, efficient and stable diflavin reudctase with a broad substrate spectrum, which is able to support CYP106A and CYP21 in vitro and in whole-cell biotranformation systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BmCpr is a novel NADPH-dependent cytochrome p450 reductase that is capable of supporting the activity of both bacterial and mammalian CYPs.

we have identified, characterized and applied a novel soluble NAPH-dependent diflavin protein from B. megaterim, which is able to support the electron transfer of two P450s, and, therefore, is a promising candidate for the development of whole-cell CYP-based biotransformation processes.

we identified and characterized a novel NADPH-dependent soluble flavoprotein reductorase from Bacillus Megaterium, which is able to efficiently support the CYP106A2- and CYP 21A2-based biotransformation reactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the B. megaterum cytochrome P-450 reductase, a novel flavoprotein, can serve as a good electron donor to bacterial and microsomal Cyp450s, thus providing a new tool to study CYP-catalyzed reactions.
B. megaterum CPR (BmCPr) is a novel soluble flavoprotein that is able to support the electron transfer from NADPH to P450s.
we have identified and characterized a novel soluble NAPDH-dependent flavin reductase from B. megaterum that can be used for the efficient electron transfer to bacterial or microsomal Cyp450s.
